svg.text: Laboratory hazards, chemical waste disposal and first aid

g.text: slips and falls on a wet floor; pulling, falling
cuts from broken glassware: wear cut-resistant
gloves; dispose of broken glass in a special
container; report breakages at once
keep the bench uncrowded and a safe distance
from other workers; lab coat, safety goggles,
hair and scarves tied up (16.1)
use every chemical by its standard procedure,
knowing its particular hazards and the
precautions for safe use (hazard pictograms
on the label, Figure 16.2 as printed)
never taste or smell a compound or gas; no
food in the lab; nothing down the drain;
follow the warning signs (16.1)
allergens; infectious diseases transferred
from animals to humans; viral diseases
(Figure 16.3 as printed)
never work alone: experiments in the presence
of the instructor and staff; ask for help with
unfamiliar apparatus (16.1)

svg.text: Chemical waste disposal (16.3): never in bins or the sewer; EPA rules

g.text: 1 store
2 label
3 transfer and treat
in proper containers
for each type of waste
type of waste, date,
place of origin
at the allocated site: neutralization, precipitation,
ion exchange, oxidation or reduction

svg.text: First aid in the laboratory (16.4, Table 16.1): every lab has a first aid box

g.text: cuts: minor: remove any glass, dab methylated spirit or tincture of iodine
(disinfectants); serious: press on the cut for about 10 minutes, see a doctor
eyes: acid: wash with water, then 1% sodium bicarbonate; alkali: water,
then 1% boric acid; particle: do not rub, lift out with a soft handkerchief,
wash; soreness: a drop of olive oil, eyes closed for a while
burns: dry heat: burnol or mustard oil; blisters: ice-cold water, then
saturated sodium bicarbonate, then water; acid: water, 1% acetic acid, water,
dry, burnol; alkali: 2% ammonia, glycerin, wipe, burnol; bromine: as printed,
the table lists bromine burns without a separate treatment
poisons: swallowed: spit at once, rinse the mouth repeatedly;
acid: plenty of water, lime water or milk of magnesia; caustic
alkali: plenty of water, a glass of lemon or orange juice;
heavy-metal salt: milk or the white of an egg
fire: clothes: do not run; wrap in a blanket or dry cotton cloth,
lie down; beaker of inflammable liquid: cover with a duster or
damp cloth to cut off oxygen; spirit or oil: throw sand and sodium
bicarbonate, never water (it spreads the fire); electrical: switch
off the supply, throw sand, never water
always: report every accident or breakage to the lab in-charge at once
